soc-gen-01-c1.text: Mari Mikkola (2008). Feminist Perspectives on Sex and Gender. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-gen-01-c1.quote: the psychologist Robert Stoller (1968) began using the terms ‘sex’ to pick out biological traits and ‘gender’ to pick out the amount of femininity and masculinity a person exhibited
soc-gen-01-c1.claim: To explain why some people felt trapped in the wrong bodies, Robert Stoller began in 1968 to use sex for biological traits and gender for the amount of femininity and masculinity a person showed.

soc-gen-01-c1.text: Pınar Ferry (2015). Ann Oakley, Sex, Gender and Society. Lectures.
soc-gen-01-c1.quote: Elle y met en évidence la distinction entre sexe (donné biologique) et genre (construction sociale).
soc-gen-01-c1.claim: In Britain the distinction entered sociology through a 1972 book by Ann Oakley, written when she was 27

soc-gen-01-c2.text: Phil Gaetano (2017). David Reimer and John Money Gender Reassignment Controversy: The John/Joan Case. Embryo Project Encyclopedia.
soc-gen-01-c2.quote: Money described Reimer’s transition as successful, and claimed that Reimer’s girlish behavior stood in stark contrast to his brother’s boyishness.
soc-gen-01-c2.claim: Money described the transition as successful and contrasted the child's girlish behaviour with the twin brother's boyishness.

soc-gen-01-c3.text: Leonard Sax (2002). How common is intersex? a response to Anne Fausto-Sterling. Journal of sex research.
soc-gen-01-c3.quote: Applying this more precise definition, the true prevalence of intersex is seen to be about 0.018%
soc-gen-01-c3.claim: he put the rate at about 0.018%, almost 100 times lower

soc-gen-01-c3.text: Mari Mikkola (2008). Feminist Perspectives on Sex and Gender. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-gen-01-c3.quote: They do not deny that physical bodies exist.
soc-gen-01-c3.claim: Butler does not deny that physical bodies exist.

soc-gen-02-c1.text: Candace West, Don H. Zimmerman (1987). Doing Gender. Gender & Society.
soc-gen-02-c1.quote: Our purpose in this article is to propose an ethnomethodologically informed, and therefore distinctively sociological, understanding of gender as a routine, methodical, and recurring accomplishment.
soc-gen-02-c1.claim: They described it as a routine, methodical and recurring accomplishment, produced in everyday interaction.

soc-gen-02-c2.text: Mari Mikkola (2008). Feminist Perspectives on Sex and Gender. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-gen-02-c2.quote: It is not “a stable identity or locus of agency from which various acts follow; rather, gender is … instituted … through a stylized repetition of [habitual] acts” (Butler 1999, 179)
soc-gen-02-c2.claim: Gender is not a stable identity from which acts follow; it is instituted through a stylised repetition of habitual acts, from ways of walking and dressing to ways of speaking and desiring, repeated until they seem natural.

soc-gen-02-c2.text: Martha C. Nussbaum (1999). The Professor of Parody. The New Republic.
soc-gen-02-c2.quote: And here lies a dangerous quietism.
soc-gen-02-c2.claim: She called the result a dangerous quietism.

soc-gen-02-c3.text: Brent Pickett (2002). Homosexuality. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-gen-02-c3.quote: Thus homosexuality, as a specific sexual construction, is best understood as a solely modern, Western concept and role.
soc-gen-02-c3.claim: On this view homosexuality as a kind of person is a solely modern, Western concept and role.

soc-gen-02-c3.text: Andrea Ganna et al (2019). Large-scale GWAS reveals insights into the genetic architecture of same-sex sexual behavior. Science (New York, N.Y.).
soc-gen-02-c3.quote: We performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) on 477,522 individuals, revealing five loci significantly associated with same-sex sexual behavior.
soc-gen-02-c3.claim: In 2019 a genome-wide study of 477,522 people found five genetic loci linked to same-sex sexual behaviour.

soc-gen-03-c1.text: Noëlle McAfee, Katie B. Howard (2009). Feminist Political Philosophy. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-gen-03-c1.quote: the first wave of feminism in the English-speaking world from the 1840s to the 1920s, focused on improving the political, educational, and economic system primarily for middle-class white women
soc-gen-03-c1.claim: The first wave in the English-speaking world, from the 1840s to the 1920s, won the vote and a language of equal rights, though its campaigns were aimed mainly at middle-class white women.

soc-gen-03-c2.text: Daniel Martinez HoSang (2020). Intersectionality. Keywords for American Cultural Studies.
soc-gen-03-c2.quote: In 1976, five black women who labored on the assembly line at General Motors in St. Louis sued their employer
soc-gen-03-c2.claim: In 1976, five Black women who worked on the assembly line at General Motors in St Louis sued the company.

soc-gen-03-c2.text: Daniel Martinez HoSang (2020). Intersectionality. Keywords for American Cultural Studies.
soc-gen-03-c2.quote: permitted them to bring forth a complaint of race-based discrimination or of sex-based discrimination, but in the court’s terms, “not a combination of both.”
soc-gen-03-c2.claim: It ruled that the law let them claim race discrimination or sex discrimination, but not a combination of both.

soc-gen-03-c3.text: Amy Allen (2005). Feminist Perspectives on Power. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-gen-03-c3.quote: As Jennifer Nash has argued, this has led to “the question of whether all identities are intersectional or whether only multiply marginalized subjects have an intersectional identity” (Nash 2008, 9).
soc-gen-03-c3.claim: Jennifer Nash asked whether all identities are intersectional or only those of people marginalised in several ways at once.

soc-gen-04-c1.text: R. W. Connell, James W. Messerschmidt (2005). Hegemonic Masculinity: Rethinking the Concept. Gender & Society.
soc-gen-04-c1.quote: The concept of hegemonic masculinity was first proposed in reports from a field study of social inequality in Australian high schools (Kessler et al. 1982)
soc-gen-04-c1.claim: a field study of social inequality in Australian high schools, reported by Kessler and colleagues in 1982

soc-gen-04-c1.text: R. W. Connell, James W. Messerschmidt (2005). Hegemonic Masculinity: Rethinking the Concept. Gender & Society.
soc-gen-04-c1.quote: Hegemonic masculinity was not assumed to be normal in the statistical sense; only a minority of men might enact it.
soc-gen-04-c1.claim: Only a minority of men may actually enact it, as with the ideal of the tough, unflinching breadwinner that few men match.

soc-gen-04-c2.text: R. W. Connell, James W. Messerschmidt (2005). Hegemonic Masculinity: Rethinking the Concept. Gender & Society.
soc-gen-04-c2.quote: Five principal criticisms have been advanced since debate about the concept began in the early 1990s.
soc-gen-04-c2.claim: That year Connell and James Messerschmidt reviewed five principal criticisms that had built up since the early 1990s.

soc-gen-04-c3.text: Richard V. Reeves, Ember Smith (2022). Boys left behind: Education gender gaps across the US. Brookings.
soc-gen-04-c3.quote: In 1970, just 12 percent of young women (ages 25 to 34) had a bachelor’s degree, compared to 20 percent of men
soc-gen-04-c3.claim: In the United States in 1970, 20% of men aged 25 to 34 held a bachelor's degree against 12% of women; by 2020 the figures were 32% for men and 41% for women.

soc-gen-04-c3.text: Office for National Statistics (2025). Suicides in England and Wales: 2024 registrations. Office for National Statistics.
soc-gen-04-c3.quote: For males, the suicide rate in England and Wales remained relatively unchanged in 2024 at 17.6 suicide deaths registered per 100,000 people
soc-gen-04-c3.claim: In England and Wales in 2024, the suicide rate was 17.6 deaths per 100,000 for males and 5.7 for females, roughly three to one.

soc-gen-05-c1.text: Office for National Statistics (2026). Gender pay gap in the UK: 2026. Office for National Statistics.
soc-gen-05-c1.quote: It was 6.8% in April 2026, down from 7.2% in April 2025. This compares with 9.4% a decade ago and 16.4% 25 years ago.
soc-gen-05-c1.claim: In April 2026 it was 6.8% for full-time employees, down from 7.2% in April 2025, 9.4% a decade earlier and 16.4% in 2001.

soc-gen-05-c1.text: Office for National Statistics (2026). Gender pay gap in the UK: 2026. Office for National Statistics.
soc-gen-05-c1.quote: It is a measure across all jobs in the UK, not of the difference in pay between men and women for doing the same job.
soc-gen-05-c1.claim: The ONS figure is a measure across all jobs, not a comparison of men and women doing the same job.

soc-gen-05-c1.text: OECD (2025). LMF1.5: Gender pay gaps for full-time workers and earnings differentials by educational attainment. OECD Family Database.
soc-gen-05-c1.quote: In 2024 (or latest available year), the gender gap in median earnings ranged from as high as 29.0% in Korea to as low as -8.4% in Luxembourg
soc-gen-05-c1.claim: Internationally, the gap in median full-time earnings across OECD countries in 2024 (or the latest year) averaged 10.1%, ranging from 29.0% in Korea to negative 8.4% in Luxembourg.

soc-gen-05-c2.text: Francine D. Blau, Lawrence M. Kahn (2016). The Gender Wage Gap: Extent, Trends, and Explanations. NBER Working Paper 21913.
soc-gen-05-c2.quote: By 2010, conventional human capital variables taken together explained little of the gender wage gap, while gender differences in occupation and industry continued to be important.
soc-gen-05-c2.claim: By 2010, conventional human capital variables such as education and experience explained little of it, while differences in occupation and industry remained important.

soc-gen-05-c3.text: Dan Aloi (2005). Mothers face disadvantages in getting hired, Cornell study says. Cornell Chronicle.
soc-gen-05-c3.quote: participants said they would hire 84 percent of the women without children, compared with only 47 percent of the mothers.
soc-gen-05-c3.claim: Participants said they would hire 84% of the women without children but only 47% of the mothers, and offered the women without children an average of $11,000 more in starting salary.

soc-gen-05-c3.text: Gender Action Portal (2007). Getting a Job: Is There a Motherhood Penalty?. Gender Action Portal, Harvard Kennedy School.
soc-gen-05-c3.quote: They receive 2.1 times as many callbacks as equally qualified mothers.
soc-gen-05-c3.claim: In the audit study with real employers, childless women received 2.1 times as many callbacks as equally qualified mothers.

soc-gen-06-c1.text: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (2023). Popular information: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2023. NobelPrize.org.
soc-gen-06-c1.quote: For example, it had once been common for women’s occupation to be designated as “wife” in censuses and public records
soc-gen-06-c1.claim: Census takers often recorded a married woman's occupation simply as wife, missing her work on farms, in family businesses and in cottage industries.

soc-gen-06-c1.text: Claudia Goldin, Lawrence F. Katz (2012). The Most Egalitarian of All Professions: Pharmacy and the Evolution of a Family-Friendly Occupation. NBER Working Paper 18410.
soc-gen-06-c1.quote: Pharmacy has become a female-majority profession that is highly remunerated with a small gender earnings gap and low earnings dispersion relative to other occupations.
soc-gen-06-c1.claim: Goldin and Katz showed that US pharmacy became a female-majority, highly paid profession with a small gender earnings gap.

soc-gen-06-c2.text: Henrik Kleven, Camille Landais, Jakob Egholt Søgaard (2018). Children and Gender Inequality: Evidence from Denmark. NBER Working Paper 24219.
soc-gen-06-c2.quote: The arrival of children creates a gender gap in earnings of around 20% in the long run, driven in roughly equal proportions by labor force participation, hours of work, and wage rates.
soc-gen-06-c2.claim: The arrival of children created a gender gap in earnings of around 20% in the long run, coming in roughly equal parts from mothers working less often, working fewer hours and earning lower hourly wages.

soc-gen-06-c2.text: Henrik Kleven, Camille Landais, Jakob Egholt Søgaard (2020). Does Biology Drive Child Penalties? Evidence from Biological and Adoptive Families. NBER Working Paper 27130.
soc-gen-06-c2.quote: Short-run child penalties are slightly larger for biological mothers than for adoptive mothers, but their long-run child penalties are virtually identical and precisely estimated.
soc-gen-06-c2.claim: First, in Denmark, adoptive mothers' long-run penalties were virtually identical to biological mothers', which suggests that pregnancy, birth and breastfeeding are not the main driver.

soc-gen-06-c3.text: The Christian Science Monitor (1989). Taking the Gender Out of Housework. The Christian Science Monitor.
soc-gen-06-c3.quote: So time-consuming are those responsibilities that the women in her study spent an average of an extra month a year in unpaid work at home.
soc-gen-06-c3.claim: She found that employed wives still did about 75% of household tasks on average, and that the women in her study put in an average of an extra month a year of unpaid work at home.

soc-gen-06-c3.text: Michael Burda, Daniel S. Hamermesh, Philippe Weil (2007). Total Work, Gender and Social Norms. NBER Working Paper 13000.
soc-gen-06-c3.quote: In rich northern countries on four continents, including the United States, there is no difference -- men and women do the same amount of total work.
soc-gen-06-c3.claim: When the economists Michael Burda, Daniel Hamermesh and Philippe Weil added paid and unpaid work together, using time diaries from 25 countries, they found that in rich northern countries, including the United States, men and women do the same amount of total work on average.

soc-gen-07-c1.text: Gijsbert Stoet, David C. Geary (2018). The Gender-Equality Paradox in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics Education. Psychological science.
soc-gen-07-c1.quote: Paradoxically, the sex differences in the magnitude of relative academic strengths and pursuit of STEM degrees rose with increases in national gender equality.
soc-gen-07-c1.claim: Yet the sex gap in pursuing STEM degrees grew, rather than shrank, with national gender equality.

soc-gen-07-c2.text: Colleen Flaherty (2020). STEM's ongoing sex-difference debate. Inside Higher Ed.
soc-gen-07-c2.quote: For example, in Poland, 43.63 percent of STEM graduates are women, which would place it fifth for representation of women in STEM out of the 45 countries included in Stoet and Geary’s analysis.
soc-gen-07-c2.claim: Poland, for example, had 43.63% women among its STEM graduates, which would rank it fifth of the 45 countries in the study, yet the paper reported a value of 26.9%.

soc-gen-07-c2.text: Stephanie M. Lee (2020). A Controversial Study Claimed To Explain Why Women Don't Go Into Science And Tech. It Just Got Corrected. BuzzFeed News.
soc-gen-07-c2.quote: In December 2019, a lengthy 1,113-word correction was added to the paper, clarifying how the researchers had arrived at their conclusions and correcting several sentences and misleading figures.
soc-gen-07-c2.claim: A December 2019 correction of 1,113 words explained that they had used a propensity measure, which can be read as the percentage of women in STEM if equal numbers of men and women enrolled at university.

soc-gen-07-c3.text: Office for National Statistics (2023). Gender identity, England and Wales: Census 2021. Office for National Statistics.
soc-gen-07-c3.quote: A total of 262,000 people (0.5%) answered “No”, indicating that their gender identity was different from their sex registered at birth.
soc-gen-07-c3.claim: About 45.4 million people (93.5%) said yes, 262,000 (0.5%) said no, and 6.0% did not answer.

soc-gen-07-c3.text: The Supreme Court of the United Kingdom (2025). For Women Scotland Ltd (Appellant) v The Scottish Ministers (Respondent) [2025] UKSC 16. The Supreme Court.
soc-gen-07-c3.quote: The meaning of the terms “sex”, “man” and “woman” in the EA 2010 is biological and not certificated sex.
soc-gen-07-c3.claim: On 16 April 2025 the UK Supreme Court ruled that the terms sex, man and woman in the Equality Act 2010 refer to biological sex, not certificated sex.
